modules.name: shared-config
owns: the positive-integer parsing rule for the PORT environment variable
public entry point index.ts re-exporting IPortResolver, PortResolver, DEFAULT_PORT

modules.name: bootstrap
owns: src/index.ts — the process entry point (composition root)
reading process.env.PORT and resolving it through IPortResolver
the startup log line, which must name the port actually bound

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — shared-config module: IPortResolver + PortResolver + DEFAULT_PORT
recommended_phases.rationale: Create src/shared/config/ with port-resolver.interface.ts (IPortResolver.resolvePort(rawPort) declared BEFORE any implementation), port-resolver.ts (PortResolver + exported DEFAULT_PORT = 3000), and index.ts as the public entry point. The parsing rule lives here and nowhere else: undefined/empty/non-numeric/non-positive-integer -> DEFAULT_PORT; a valid positive integer -> that number. No dependency on Fastify, the app instance, or process.env (the caller passes the raw value), so the module is pure and unit-testable. This is the only phase that introduces new symbols; everything else consumes it.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — wire src/index.ts to the resolver and keep the startup log accurate
recommended_phases.rationale: Rewrite src/index.ts to resolve the port through the shared-config public entry point (import { PortResolver } from './shared/config') instead of the hardcoded const PORT = 3000, and pass the resolved value to app.listen({ port, host: '0.0.0.0' }). The startup log line must interpolate the SAME resolved value that was passed to listen, so it stays accurate for whichever port is actually used. Keep the existing try/catch, app.log.error(err) and process.exit(1) failure path unchanged. No other file changes; src/app.ts is untouched.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — unit tests for the PORT resolution rule
recommended_phases.rationale: Add tests/unit/shared/config.test.ts (Jest, matching the existing tests/unit/shared/ layout and jest.config.js testMatch) covering the three required cases against PortResolver.resolvePort: PORT unset (undefined -> 3000), PORT set to a valid value (e.g. '8080' -> 8080), and PORT set to a non-numeric value (e.g. 'abc' -> 3000). Add the boundary cases the rule implies — '0', '-1', '3000.5', '' and whitespace — all falling back to 3000, plus a valid value that is not the default to prove the fallback is not unconditional. Assert DEFAULT_PORT is 3000 so the fallback value has one pinned source. No production source changes.

app_notes:
Layers. Presentation: none — this feature adds no route, no controller, and no API surface. Application: `IPortResolver` / `PortResolver` in the new `shared-config` module (`src/shared/config/`), the only new service; `resolvePort(rawPort)` is declared on the interface before the implementation, and the implementation is referenced by its consumer only through the interface. Domain: none — no entity, no lifecycle state, no repository, no table; the feature is pure configuration resolution. Infrastructure: `src/index.ts` (the `bootstrap` module) is the composition root that reads `process.env.PORT`, constructs the resolver, and passes the resolved value to `app.listen`; `src/app.ts` (the `app` module) is untouched.

Dependency direction. `bootstrap -> shared-config` and `bootstrap -> app`; `shared-config -> shared-errors` (only if the out-of-range open question resolves to a thrown error — otherwise `shared-config` has zero dependencies and is a leaf). All edges point inward toward shared foundations; nothing depends on `bootstrap`, and `shared-config` depends on no domain module. No cycles: the graph is a two-node fan-out from `bootstrap` plus one optional leaf edge, verified before returning.

Shared value-type placement. No new enum, DTO, or methodless interface is introduced, so nothing is added to `src/shared/types/`. `DEFAULT_PORT` is a constant, not a type, and is owned by the module that applies the rule (`shared-config`), not by `shared/types`. `IPortResolver` declares a method, so it is a service interface and correctly gets its own module directory rather than a place in `shared/types/`.

Concern about the existing architecture (surfaced, not silently resolved). `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s module map covers domain modules (`leave`, `balance`, `employee`, `policy`, `notification`, `audit`, `validation`, `leave-type`) and shared foundations (`shared/types`, `shared/errors`, `shared/db`, `shared/date`, `shared/auth`). It does not describe `src/index.ts` or `src/app.ts` at all — the process entry point and the Fastify composition root are outside the documented module map, and `HARNESS.json`'s `applicationRoots` containers (`modules`, `shared`) likewise have no slot for a bootstrap concern. This feature is the first to touch the entry point, so it extends the map with two entries the document has no precedent for: a `bootstrap` module at `src/` and a new `shared-config` foundation. That is an extension, not a contradiction, but the document should record both so the next entry-point change has a home. Second, smaller concern: the codebase's service-file convention is `<name>.service.interface.ts` + `<name>.service.ts` (see `uptime`, the closest precedent for a trivial stateless service), whereas this design names the files `port-resolver.interface.ts` / `port-resolver.ts` to match the `shared/` foundation convention (`shared/db/unit-of-work.ts`, `shared/date/accrual.ts`). Both are defensible; the design agent should pick one and apply it consistently rather than mixing the two within the module.

Foundational computation semantics. The PORT validity predicate is the one derived rule in this feature and it must hold for every caller of `resolvePort`, so it is recorded as an open question (out-of-range ports) rather than baked silently into the implementation. The fallback value itself is not open: `DEFAULT_PORT = 3000` is a single exported constant owned by `shared-config`, so no second copy of `3000` can drift.

open_questions.question: Where should the PORT resolution rule live — a new shared-config module (src/shared/config/) or a module-local helper inside src/index.ts?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the rule is unit-testable in isolation and whether a future env-var (HOST, LOG_LEVEL, DATABASE_URL-style config) has an established home. src/index.ts is the process entry point and is not imported by any test today, so a helper defined there can only be tested by importing the entry point (which calls app.listen and starts a real server). The chosen option is the shared-config module, which keeps src/index.ts a thin composition root and matches the existing src/shared/<concern>/index.ts convention (shared/db, shared/date, shared/auth, shared/errors).
candidate_options: New shared-config module src/shared/config/ with IPortResolver + PortResolver + DEFAULT_PORT (chosen)
Inline helper function in src/index.ts, tested by extracting it to a separate file later
Extend src/shared/db/connection.ts-style env handling into a general src/shared/env/ module covering PORT and future variables

open_questions.question: Should an out-of-range but syntactically valid PORT (e.g. '70000', above 65535) fall back to 3000 or be passed through to app.listen and fail at bind time?
open_questions.impact: The feature description specifies only 'unset or not a positive integer', so 70000 is technically a positive integer and would be passed through, producing a bind failure and process.exit(1) rather than a silent fallback to 3000. The two behaviours differ observably: fallback hides a misconfiguration, pass-through surfaces it loudly. This is a foundational computation rule (the validity predicate for PORT) that must hold for every caller of resolvePort, so it must not be decided silently inside one method.
candidate_options: Pass through any positive integer; let app.listen fail on an out-of-range port (literal reading of the requirement)
Treat > 65535 as invalid and fall back to 3000 (extend the validity predicate to the TCP port range)
Treat > 65535 as invalid and throw a ValidationError at startup instead of falling back

open_questions.question: Should the resolved port be logged via console.log (as today) or through the Fastify logger (app.log.info), and does the startup log line need to change shape?
open_questions.impact: The requirement says 'keep the existing startup log line accurate for whichever port is actually used', which fixes the message content but not the sink. src/index.ts currently uses console.log while src/app.ts configures Fastify with logger: true, so the startup line is the one message that bypasses the structured logger. Changing the sink is a behaviour change beyond the stated scope; leaving it means the port is absent from structured logs. Either way the interpolated value must be the same resolved value passed to app.listen.
candidate_options: Keep console.log with the same message text, only the interpolated port changes (minimal, matches the requirement literally)
Switch to app.log.info so the startup line joins the structured logger
Log both: console.log for the human-readable line and app.log.info for the structured record
